description: The SDD spec for the MCP server itself. The server that teaches spec-driven development is built spec-first: every requirement below is implemented, has tagged Gherkin scenarios in the feature file (BDD level, run by Cucumber), and is covered by unit tests (TDD level, JUnit) at 100% instruction and branch coverage. SpecCompletenessTest fails the build if this spec and the feature file drift apart.

requirements.title: Agents can list every requirement
requirements.story: As an agent, I want to list all requirements with id, title, and status so that I can find pending work.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a loaded spec, when list_requirements is called, then every requirement's id, title, and status is returned
Given a loaded spec, when list_requirements is called, then the project name is included

requirements.title: Agents can fetch one requirement's acceptance criteria
requirements.story: As an agent, I want one requirement's story, acceptance criteria, and file locations so that I can write its Gherkin scenario and failing tests first.
acceptanceCriteria: Given an existing requirement id, when get_requirement is called, then its acceptance criteria and a workflow hint naming the @tag are returned
Given an unknown requirement id, when get_requirement is called, then the result is a tool error that points at list_requirements

requirements.title: run_tests reports one bar for BDD and TDD together
requirements.story: As an agent, I want to run the kata suite and get a single RED or GREEN answer so that Cucumber scenarios and JUnit tests share one bar.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a passing suite, when run_tests is called, then the phase is GREEN
Given a failing suite, when run_tests is called, then the phase is RED and the failure details are included
Given a build that fails before tests run, when run_tests is called, then the phase is RED and the build output is included

requirements.title: Agents can ask where they are in the cycle
requirements.story: As an agent, I want the current Red/Green/Refactor phase, the last run summary, and a suggested next step so that I always know what to do next.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a recorded test run, when get_tdd_state is called, then the phase, last run counts, refactor log, and a next step are returned

requirements.title: Refactoring is only allowed on a green bar
requirements.story: As the workflow guardian, I want start_refactor to refuse on a red bar so that the discipline lives in the tool, not in the prompt.
acceptanceCriteria: Given the bar is GREEN, when start_refactor is called, then the phase becomes REFACTOR and the note is logged
Given the bar is RED, when start_refactor is called, then the result is a tool error that names the red bar rule

requirements.title: The server exposes exactly the seven workflow tools
requirements.story: As an MCP host, I want the server to identify itself and expose the seven workflow tools so that any client can discover and drive the loop.
acceptanceCriteria: Given an assembled server, when its identity is read, then it identifies as tdd-workflow-server version 1.0.0

Given the tool specifications, when their names are listed, then they are exactly list_requirements, get_requirement, validate_spec, refine_requirement, run_tests, get_tdd_state, start_refactor in workflow order

requirements.title: Agents can validate the spec and iterate until it is valid
requirements.story: As an agent drafting requirements with the developer, I want to validate the spec after every edit so that we iterate to a valid spec before any scenario or code is written.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a valid spec on disk, when validate_spec is called, then valid is true and the next step points at get_requirement
Given an invalid spec on disk, when validate_spec is called, then valid is false and every issue is listed with the requirement id it belongs to
Given a spec edited since the server started, when validate_spec is called, then the file is re-read fresh from disk

requirements.title: Agents can get wording feedback and refine a requirement
requirements.story: As an agent refining a requirement with the developer, I want deterministic quality feedback on its wording so that I can reword and re-check until the requirement is unambiguous and testable.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a well-worded requirement, when refine_requirement is called for it, then clean is true and the next step hands off to writing the Gherkin scenario
Given a vaguely worded requirement, when refine_requirement is called for it, then clean is false and each finding names what to reword
Given an unknown requirement id, when refine_requirement is called, then the call fails as a tool error pointing at list_requirements

requirements.title: The spec is a catalog that may include child spec files
requirements.story: As a developer growing a spec beyond one file, I want requirements.json to include child spec files (nested N levels deep) so that the backlog scales while one catalog stays the entry point.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a root spec including a child spec file, when list_requirements is called, then the merged backlog carries the requirements of every file in catalog order
Given an include cycle in the spec tree, when validate_spec is called, then the issue names the file that is included more than once
Given the same requirement id declared in two files, when validate_spec is called, then the duplicate issue names the file that declared it first
